polozky.nadpis: How Drone Surveys Expand What’s Surveyable From the Air
polozky.perex: Ten years ago, an aerial survey usually meant a manned aircraft, a mobilisation cost that ruled out anything but the largest jobs.
polozky.telo: Ten years ago, an aerial survey usually meant a manned aircraft, a mobilisation cost that ruled out anything but the largest jobs. Drones changed the economics fast, and most of the conversation since has been about speed: faster mobilisation, faster processing, lower cost per hectare. The bigger shift is what UAV survey platforms have done for sites that were once barely surveyable at all. Reaching What Was Once Off-Limits Until recently, a coastal slope that had just failed, a quarry face still being cut, or a flood-damaged corridor with no stable ground to stand on simply didn’t get surveyed to the same standard as a stable site. polozky.telo: Gaussian splatting is rapidly gaining attention as a new way to create highly realistic 3D representations from imagery. We will also compare Gaussian splats with traditional textured meshes and discuss when each approach makes sense.
